title: What is science?
competency: Define science and tell indigenous science from conventional science, with Ethiopian examples.

keywords.def: A systematic way of learning about the natural and physical world and human society, based on observation and evidence.
Knowledge that local people build from long experience of their environment, based on social, physical and spiritual understanding.
Knowledge based on laws found by using the scientific method on events in the world. Often called Western science.
An orderly way to find out: observe, test, and check the evidence.
A plant that people use for treating and curing diseases, such as the kosso tree.

en.text: The word science comes from the Latin word scientia, meaning knowledge. But science is more than having knowledge. It is an orderly way of learning about nature and human society. It is based on observation and evidence.

am.text: ሳይንስ የሚለው ቃል ‹ሳይንሺያ› ከሚለው የላቲን ቃል የመጣ ሲሆን ትርጉሙ እውቀት ነው። ሳይንስ ግን እውቀት ከመያዝ በላይ ነው። ስለ ተፈጥሮና ስለ ሰው ማህበረሰብ በሥርዓት የምንማርበት መንገድ ነው። በምልከታና በማስረጃ ላይ የተመሠረተ ነው።

screens.title: Will it rain?
screens.text: Your grandmother says dark clouds over Entoto mean rain. You want to know if she is right.
opts: Watch the clouds and record the rain for many days
screens.after: A scientist watches carefully and collects evidence. Then she decides. Read on.

screens.title: Science in Grade 7
paras: In lower grades you learnt science in general, like environmental science.
In Grades 7 and 8 you study General Science. It is about your daily life.

screens.title: Where the word comes from
paras: Science comes from the Latin word scientia. Scientia means "knowledge".
But science is more than knowledge. It is a systematic (orderly) way of gaining it.

screens.title: What science studies
paras: Science studies the physical and natural world and human society.
It shows what things are like. It is based on observation and evidence.

screens.title: Science is a way of knowing
defs: A systematic method of gaining knowledge about the physical and natural world and human society. It is based on observation and evidence.

screens.title: More than knowledge
screens.text: Why is science more than "having knowledge"?
opts: It is only what happens in laboratories
It is guessing until you are right
It is an orderly way of getting knowledge, based on observation and evidence
screens.ans: It is an orderly way of getting knowledge, based on observation and evidence
screens.why: Science is a systematic method, not only a store of facts.
screens.clue: Look for the words "systematic method" and "evidence" in the text.

screens.title: The Latin root
screens.ask: The word science comes from the Latin word ___, which means knowledge.
screens.why: Science comes from scientia, the Latin word for knowledge.
screens.clue: It is a Latin word that starts like "science".

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: Science is based on observation and evidence.
screens.why: Science is a way of learning what things are like, based on observation and evidence.

screens.title: Teff seeds
screens.text: Almaz plants teff seeds in wet soil and in dry soil. Each day she counts the seeds that sprout and writes the numbers.
opts: No, because she is not in a laboratory
Yes, because she gathers evidence by observing in an orderly way
No, because she already knows the answer
Yes, because she memorised a fact
screens.ans: Yes, because she gathers evidence by observing in an orderly way
screens.why: Science is a systematic way of learning, based on observation and evidence. Almaz observes and records.
screens.clue: Does science need a laboratory, or does it need orderly observation?
screens.worked: Almaz observes the seeds each day and records numbers. That is evidence collected in an orderly way. So yes, she is doing science.

en.text: Science can be indigenous or conventional. Indigenous science is knowledge local people build from long experience of their environment. Conventional science relies on laws found with the scientific method. It is often called Western science.

am.text: ሳይንስ ሀገር በቀል ወይም ዘመናዊ ሊሆን ይችላል። ሀገር በቀል ሳይንስ የአካባቢው ሰዎች ከአካባቢያቸው ጋር ባላቸው ረጅም ልምድ የሚገነቡት እውቀት ነው። ዘመናዊ ሳይንስ በሳይንሳዊ ዘዴ በተገኙ ሕጎች ላይ ይመሠረታል። ብዙ ጊዜ የምዕራባውያን ሳይንስ ይባላል።

screens.title: Keeping grain safe
screens.text: A family has kept grain safe for generations. They use local methods learnt from their elders.
screens.why: It is knowledge built from local people's long experience of their environment.
screens.clue: Which kind of science comes from local people and their surroundings?
screens.ask: This is mainly an example of:

screens.title: Frost in the highlands
screens.text: A farmer near Debre Birhan looks at the night sky. He says frost will come. His father taught him this sign.
screens.why: The knowledge comes from local experience passed down in his family.
screens.clue: Did he learn it from a laboratory law, or from his elders?
screens.ask: Which kind of knowledge is he using?
screens.worked: He did not use laws found in a laboratory. He used local knowledge passed down from his father. So it is indigenous science.

en.text: We learn indigenous knowledge for two reasons. It makes us aware of our own culture and identity. It also lets us join it with Western science. In Ethiopia, people make medicine from plants and preserve meat with salt and smoke drying.

am.text: ሀገር በቀል እውቀትን የምንማረው በሁለት ምክንያቶች ነው። ስለ ራሳችን ባህልና ማንነት እንድናውቅ ያደርገናል። ከምዕራባውያን ሳይንስ ጋር እንድናጣምረውም ያስችለናል። በኢትዮጵያ ሰዎች ከተክሎች መድኃኒት ይሠራሉ፤ ሥጋንም በጨውና በጭስ በማድረቅ ያቆያሉ።

screens.title: Before fridges
screens.text: Long ago, villages in Ethiopia had no fridges. Meat goes bad in a few days.
screens.ask: How do you think families kept meat for a long time?
opts: Leaving it wet in the sun
screens.after: Families used salt and smoke drying. This is indigenous knowledge. Read on.

screens.title: Why learn indigenous knowledge?
paras: First, it makes us more aware of our own culture and identity.
Second, it lets us join indigenous knowledge with Western science.

screens.title: Indigenous knowledge in Ethiopia
paras: Ethiopia has a wide variety of indigenous knowledge. People long used it to solve practical problems.
One example is medicine from plants against disease and infection. Another is preserving meat with salt and smoke drying.

screens.caption: Medicinal plants treat and cure diseases.

screens.title: Medicinal plants
paras: People use these plants for treating and curing diseases.
screens.note: Never use a plant as medicine unless a health worker tells you how.

screens.title: Plants that heal
defs: A plant that people use for treating and curing diseases. Kosso, bahrzaf and damakese are examples.

screens.title: Spot the example
screens.text: Which is an example of Ethiopian indigenous knowledge?
opts: Heating liquid with a Bunsen burner
Using kosso, bahrzaf or damakese plants to treat illness
Using a microscope to see cells
screens.ans: Using kosso, bahrzaf or damakese plants to treat illness
screens.why: These plants have been used by local people for a long time to treat disease.
screens.clue: Think about knowledge that comes from local plants and people.

screens.title: A sick cousin
screens.text: Hanna's cousin feels sick. Hanna should boil damakese leaves and give them to him without asking anyone.
screens.why: Never use a plant as medicine unless a health worker or a knowledgeable adult tells you how.
screens.clue: Read the safety note under the plant table.
screens.worked: The book lists damakese as a medicinal plant. But it does not say how to use it. The safety note says: ask a health worker or a knowledgeable adult first. So the statement is false.

notes.text: The printed book has no heading "1.1.1". It jumps from "1.1" to the introduction. The heading is added so the numbering matches 1.1.2, 1.1.3 and 1.1.4.
Modern science has grown from the work of people in many cultures, so "Western" is only a common label, not the whole story.
The book does not say which diseases each plant treats. Never use a plant as medicine unless a health worker or a knowledgeable adult tells you how.
Hooks and the word problems marked "added" are not in the book; they use Ethiopian settings to introduce the book's ideas.
